userPrompt: Does the GDPR let me keep customer data forever if I got consent once?
responseText:
**No.**

GDPR does **not** let you keep customer data forever just because you obtained consent once.

### Key reasons:

- **Consent must be informed and specific.**  
  You must tell the data subject **how long** you will keep their data (Art. 13/14). Saying “forever” or not specifying a period usually makes the consent invalid.

- **Withdrawal of consent.**  
  The data subject can withdraw consent at any time (Art. 7(3)). Once they do, you must stop processing and, in most cases, delete the data. You cannot rely on “I got consent once” after withdrawal.

- **Storage limitation principle (Art. 5(1)(e)).**  
  Personal data must be kept “no longer than is necessary for the purposes for which they were collected.”  
  Even with valid consent, you still need a **documented retention period** or clear criteria for when you will delete the data. “Forever” or “indefinitely” almost always violates this principle.

- **Legitimate ongoing interest or legal obligation** may allow longer retention in narrow cases, but not based on one-time consent.

### Practical rule of thumb:
- State a concrete retention period (e.g., “3 years after last purchase” or “until consent is withdrawn, reviewed every 2 years”).
- Re-obtain fresh consent or switch to another lawful basis (contract, legitimate interest) when the original purpose ends or consent is withdrawn.
- Document everything.

If you want to keep data for a very long time (e.g., lifetime value, research, archiving), you usually need a different lawful basis + strict anonymisation/pseudonymisation + a defensible justification. One-time consent is almost never enough.
